topic: charger forgotten at a friend's place
title: Un cargador olvidado
text:
Camila: Sofi, creo que anoche dejé el cargador del celular en tu casa. ¿Lo viste?
Sofía: Sí, aquí está. Lo encontré esta mañana debajo del sofá, cuando estaba barriendo.
Camila: ¡Qué alivio! Pensé que lo había dejado en el taxi.
Sofía: Si quieres, te lo llevo a la universidad. Tengo clase a las diez.
Camila: A esa hora estoy trabajando. ¿Puedo pasar por tu casa al mediodía?
Sofía: Listo, pero no llegues tarde: a la una salgo para donde mi abuela.
translation:
Camila: Sofi, I think I left my phone charger at your place last night. Did you see it?
Sofía: Yes, it's here. I found it this morning under the sofa while I was sweeping.
Camila: What a relief! I thought I'd left it in the taxi.
Sofía: If you want, I'll bring it to the university for you. I have class at ten.
Camila: I'm working at that time. Can I stop by your place at noon?
Sofía: OK, but don't be late: at one I'm leaving for my grandma's.

questions.q: Why does Camila write to Sofía?
options: To invite Sofía to lunch today
To ask for a ride to the university
To ask about her missing charger
To plan a visit to Sofía's grandma
questions.explain: Camila writes 'creo que anoche dejé el cargador del celular en tu casa. ¿Lo viste?'

questions.q: Where did Sofía find the charger?
options: In a taxi
Under the sofa
At the university
In her bedroom
questions.explain: Sofía writes 'Lo encontré esta mañana debajo del sofá'.

questions.q: What will Camila probably do at noon?
options: Have lunch at the university
Look for the charger in the taxi
Go with Sofía to her grandmother's
Go to Sofía's place to get it
questions.explain: Camila asks '¿Puedo pasar por tu casa al mediodía?' and Sofía answers 'Listo'.

topic: a Spanish visitor orders a tinto
title: Un tinto, por favor
text:
Javier, un profesor de Madrid, llegó a Bogotá un jueves para un congreso. Esa tarde salió a caminar por La Candelaria y entró a una cafetería. Allí pidió un tinto.

El mesero le trajo una taza pequeña de café negro. Javier la miró confundido, porque en España un tinto es una copa de vino. Cuando se lo explicó al mesero, los dos se rieron. El café, por cierto, estaba delicioso.

Esa noche, en un restaurante, Javier pidió «vino tinto», con todas las letras.
translation:
Javier, a teacher from Madrid, arrived in Bogotá on a Thursday for a conference. That afternoon he went for a walk around La Candelaria and went into a café. There he ordered a “tinto.”

The waiter brought him a small cup of black coffee. Javier looked at it, confused, because in Spain a “tinto” is a glass of wine. When he explained this to the waiter, they both laughed. The coffee, by the way, was delicious.

That night, at a restaurant, Javier ordered “vino tinto” (red wine), spelling it out in full.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A teacher's first class in Bogotá
A tourist who gets lost downtown
A waiter who forgets someone's order
A funny misunderstanding over one word
questions.explain: Javier orders 'un tinto', gets something he did not expect, and he and the waiter laugh about it.

questions.q: Why did Javier travel to Bogotá?
options: For a conference
To visit his family
To teach a course
For a holiday
questions.explain: The text says he came to Bogotá 'para un congreso'.

questions.q: What does the last sentence suggest?
options: He did not like Colombian coffee
He was still confused about the word
He wanted to be sure he got wine
He wanted another small black coffee
questions.explain: After getting a coffee when he asked for 'un tinto', that night he said 'vino tinto', 'con todas las letras', to be sure he got wine.

topic: building notice about a water cut
title: Suspensión del servicio de agua
text:
EDIFICIO LOS ALMENDROS
AVISO: SUSPENSIÓN DEL SERVICIO DE AGUA

Señores residentes:
Les informamos que el martes 17 de noviembre no habrá agua en el edificio entre las 8:00 a. m. y las 3:00 p. m., porque se van a lavar y desinfectar los tanques.
Les recomendamos guardar agua desde el lunes en la noche. Cuando vuelva el servicio, el agua puede salir un poco turbia: déjenla correr unos minutos antes de usarla.

Agradecemos su comprensión.
La Administración
translation:
LOS ALMENDROS BUILDING
NOTICE: WATER SERVICE INTERRUPTION

Dear residents,
We would like to inform you that on Tuesday, November 17, there will be no water in the building between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., because the tanks are going to be washed and disinfected.
We recommend storing water starting Monday night. When the service comes back, the water may come out a little cloudy: let it run for a few minutes before using it.

Thank you for your understanding.
The Management

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To ask residents to pay the water bill
To warn residents about a water cut
To explain how to save water at home
To announce new rules for the gym
questions.explain: The notice is about a 'suspensión del servicio de agua' in the building.

questions.q: Why will there be no water?
options: A pipe in the street has to be repaired
New bathrooms are being installed
The city asked everyone to use less water
The building's tanks will be cleaned
questions.explain: The notice says 'se van a lavar y desinfectar los tanques'.

questions.q: A resident needs water to cook lunch on Tuesday. What should she do?
options: Fill some containers on Monday night
Wait until the water comes back at noon
Ask the administration for bottled water
Cook with water from the lobby tap
questions.explain: There is no water from 8:00 a. m. to 3:00 p. m., and the notice recommends 'guardar agua desde el lunes en la noche'.

topic: unblocking a bank card
title: La tarjeta bloqueada
text:
—Buenos días. Ayer intenté sacar plata del cajero y se me bloqueó la tarjeta.
—¿Digitó mal la clave varias veces?
—Sí, tres veces. Es que la cambié la semana pasada y se me olvidó.
—Tranquila, eso pasa mucho. ¿Me presta su cédula, por favor?
—Claro, aquí está.
—Listo, ya le desbloqueé la tarjeta. Ahora digite una clave nueva en este teclado. Escoja cuatro números fáciles de recordar, pero no use su año de nacimiento.
—Perfecto. Esta vez no se me va a olvidar.
translation:
—Good morning. Yesterday I tried to take out money from the ATM, and my card got blocked.
—Did you type in the wrong PIN several times?
—Yes, three times. The thing is, I changed it last week and forgot it.
—Don't worry, that happens a lot. May I have your ID card, please?
—Of course, here it is.
—All right, I've unblocked your card. Now type a new PIN on this keypad. Choose four numbers that are easy to remember, but don't use the year you were born.
—Perfect. This time I won't forget it.

questions.q: Why does the woman go to the bank?
options: She can't use her bank card
She wants to open an account
She wants to ask for a loan
She needs to change her address
questions.explain: She says that at the ATM 'se me bloqueó la tarjeta'.

questions.q: Why did she forget her PIN?
options: Someone else had changed it
She hadn't used it in months
She had changed it recently
She lost the paper with it
questions.explain: She explains 'la cambié la semana pasada y se me olvidó'.

questions.q: Why does the employee ask for her cédula?
options: To give her a new bank card
To make sure it's her card
To type her new PIN for her
To open a savings account
questions.explain: The employee asks for her 'cédula' before unblocking the card, to check that the customer is its owner.

topic: teaching grandmother to make video calls
title: La abuela y el celular
text:
Mi abuela Carmen tiene 79 años y vive sola en Tunja. El mes pasado le regalaron un celular nuevo, y yo le enseñé a hacer videollamadas para vernos más seguido.

Al principio fue difícil: ponía el celular tan cerca de la cara que yo solo le veía la nariz. Pero aprendió rápido.

Ahora me llama casi todas las noches, y ya les manda a todos sus nietos mensajes de buenos días con flores... a las cinco de la mañana.
translation:
My grandmother Carmen is 79 years old and lives alone in Tunja. Last month she was given a new cell phone, and I taught her to make video calls so that we could see each other more often.

At first it was hard: she held the phone so close to her face that I could only see her nose. But she learned fast.

Now she calls me almost every night, and she already sends all her grandchildren good-morning messages with flowers... at five in the morning.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A grandmother who moves in with her family
A family trip to visit relatives in Tunja
A grandmother who learns to use her phone
A grandchild who breaks a new cell phone
questions.explain: The narrator says 'le enseñé a hacer videollamadas' and tells how Carmen's first weeks with the phone went.

questions.q: What was the problem at first?
options: She could not hear her grandchild's voice
She kept forgetting to charge the phone
The phone's screen was too small for her
She held the phone too close to her face
questions.explain: The text says she held the phone 'tan cerca de la cara que yo solo le veía la nariz'.

questions.q: What can we conclude about Carmen now?
options: She uses her new phone with confidence
She still needs help to make calls
She only calls her grandchild on Sundays
She would rather write letters by hand
questions.explain: 'Aprendió rápido': now she calls 'casi todas las noches' and sends messages to all her grandchildren.

topic: changing hotel booking dates
title: Cambio de fechas
text:
Asunto: Cambio de fechas de una reserva

Buenos días:
Mi nombre es Laura Méndez y tengo una reserva en su hotel del 18 al 22 de junio, para dos personas. Ayer la aerolínea me cambió el vuelo y ahora voy a llegar a Santa Marta el 19 en la noche.
¿Sería posible cambiar la reserva del 19 al 23? En caso de que el cambio tenga un costo adicional, les agradezco que me avisen antes.
Quedo atenta a su respuesta.
Laura Méndez
translation:
Subject: Change of dates for a booking

Good morning,
My name is Laura Méndez, and I have a booking at your hotel from June 18 to 22 for two people. Yesterday the airline changed my flight, and now I'm going to arrive in Santa Marta on the 19th at night.
Would it be possible to change the booking to the 19th through the 23rd? If the change has an extra cost, I would appreciate it if you let me know beforehand.
I look forward to your reply.
Laura Méndez

questions.q: Why does Laura write to the hotel?
options: To book a second room for her friends
To ask to change the dates of her stay
To complain about the price of her room
To ask for help with a lost suitcase
questions.explain: Laura asks '¿Sería posible cambiar la reserva...?'

questions.q: What happened with Laura's flight?
options: The airline changed it
She missed it yesterday
It was cancelled for good
She could not pay for it
questions.explain: She writes 'Ayer la aerolínea me cambió el vuelo'.

questions.q: What is true about the booking Laura wants now?
options: She wants to stay one night less
She wants to arrive a day earlier
She wants the same number of nights
She wants to stay two more nights
questions.explain: The booking was 'del 18 al 22' and she asks for 'del 19 al 23': four nights both times.

topic: swapping work shifts with a colleague
title: ¿Me cambias el turno?
text:
Valentina: Hola, Felipe, ¿cómo vas? ¿Me cambiarías el turno del sábado por el del domingo? Es que me dieron cita para el examen de conducción el sábado a las diez.
Felipe: ¡Por fin vas a sacar el pase! Por mí, listo. Eso sí, el domingo me toca de seis a dos, ¿sí te sirve?
Valentina: Sí, perfecto. Mil gracias. Ya le escribo a la jefa para que cambie el horario.
Felipe: Y si pasas el examen, me invitas a un helado.
Valentina: ¡Hecho!
translation:
Valentina: Hi, Felipe, how's it going? Would you swap my Saturday shift for your Sunday one? The thing is, they gave me an appointment for my driving test on Saturday at ten.
Felipe: You're finally getting your license! It's fine by me. Just one thing: on Sunday my shift is from six to two. Does that work for you?
Valentina: Yes, perfect. Thanks a million. I'll write to the boss right now so she can change the schedule.
Felipe: And if you pass the test, you're buying me an ice cream.
Valentina: Deal!

questions.q: Why does Valentina write to Felipe?
options: To invite him for ice cream on Sunday
To tell him that their boss is angry
To tell him she is leaving the job
To ask him to swap shifts with her
questions.explain: Valentina asks '¿Me cambiarías el turno del sábado por el del domingo?'

questions.q: Why will Valentina write to their boss?
options: To ask for the whole weekend off
To say that Felipe is sick
To get the schedule changed
To ask for a higher salary
questions.explain: She writes 'Ya le escribo a la jefa para que cambie el horario'.

questions.q: Felipe writes '¡Por fin vas a sacar el pase!' What is Valentina going to get?
options: A ticket for a concert
Her driver's license
A new car from her parents
Her university diploma
questions.explain: Valentina has an 'examen de conducción', so 'sacar el pase' means getting her driver's license.

topic: recipe for ajiaco from Bogotá
title: Ajiaco santafereño
text:
AJIACO SANTAFEREÑO

1. Cocine dos pechugas de pollo y tres mazorcas en agua con sal durante media hora. Saque el pollo y desmenúcelo.
2. Agregue un kilo de papa sabanera y uno de papa pastusa, peladas y en rodajas.
3. Cuando estén blandas, añada medio kilo de papa criolla, que se deshace y le da a la sopa su textura espesa.
4. Ponga un manojo de guascas y deje hervir diez minutos más.
Sirva con el pollo, crema de leche, alcaparras y aguacate.
translation:
BOGOTÁ-STYLE AJIACO

1. Cook two chicken breasts and three ears of corn in salted water for half an hour. Take out the chicken and shred it.
2. Add a kilo of sabanera potatoes and one of pastusa potatoes, peeled and sliced.
3. When they are soft, add half a kilo of criolla potatoes, which fall apart and give the soup its thick texture.
4. Add a bunch of guascas and let it boil for ten more minutes.
Serve with the chicken, cream, capers and avocado.

questions.q: What does the text explain?
options: How to make a chicken and potato soup
How to cook rice with chicken and corn
How to make fried potatoes with sauce
How to grow different kinds of potatoes
questions.explain: It is a recipe with chicken, corn and potatoes, and it calls the dish 'la sopa'.

questions.q: When do you add the papa criolla?
options: At the very start, with the chicken
After you add the guascas
Just before you serve it
When the other potatoes are soft
questions.explain: Step 3 says 'Cuando estén blandas, añada medio kilo de papa criolla'.

questions.q: The papa criolla 'se deshace'. What happens to it?
options: It stays whole and firm
It turns dark and bitter
It falls apart as it cooks
It floats to the top of the pot
questions.explain: It 'se deshace' and gives the soup 'su textura espesa', so it breaks down as it cooks.

topic: rescheduling a dentist appointment
title: Una cita con el odontólogo
text:
—Consultorio odontológico, buenas tardes.
—Buenas tardes. Habla Andrés Rojas. Tengo cita el jueves a las cuatro para una limpieza, pero me salió un viaje de trabajo. ¿Será que me la pueden cambiar?
—Déjeme mirar la agenda... ¿Le sirve el martes a las siete de la mañana?
—Uy, muy temprano. ¿No tiene nada en la tarde?
—Solo el viernes a las cinco y media.
—Perfecto, esa me queda mejor.
—Listo. Le pido el favor de que llegue diez minutos antes para actualizar sus datos.
translation:
—Dental office, good afternoon.
—Good afternoon. This is Andrés Rojas. I have an appointment on Thursday at four for a cleaning, but a work trip has come up. Could you possibly change it for me?
—Let me check the schedule... Does Tuesday at seven in the morning work for you?
—Oh, that's very early. Don't you have anything in the afternoon?
—Only Friday at five thirty.
—Perfect, that one suits me better.
—All right. Please arrive ten minutes early to update your details.

questions.q: Why does Andrés call?
options: To cancel his work trip on Thursday
To ask about the price of a cleaning
To move his appointment to another day
To complain about a long wait
questions.explain: He has an appointment on Thursday and asks '¿Será que me la pueden cambiar?'

questions.q: Why doesn't Andrés take the Tuesday appointment?
options: It is too early in the morning
It is too late in the evening
He has to work all day on Tuesdays
The dentist is away that day
questions.explain: When he is offered Tuesday at seven in the morning, he says 'Uy, muy temprano'.

questions.q: What can we conclude about Andrés?
options: He has a terrible toothache right now
He has been a patient there before
He works as a receptionist there
He is going to cancel his trip
questions.explain: He must come early 'para actualizar sus datos', so the office already has his details.

topic: café job advert for a barista
title: Se necesita barista
text:
SE NECESITA BARISTA
Cafetería en Chapinero busca barista para los fines de semana.

Requisitos:
- Ser mayor de edad.
- Tener al menos seis meses de experiencia preparando café. No es indispensable si ha hecho un curso de barismo.
- Ser puntual y amable con los clientes.

Ofrecemos:
- Contrato por un año, salario mínimo más propinas.
- Capacitación gratuita en métodos de preparación.
Interesados, traer la hoja de vida de lunes a viernes, de 2:00 a 5:00 p. m., a la Calle 57 # 9-15.
translation:
BARISTA WANTED
A café in Chapinero is looking for a barista for weekends.

Requirements:
- Be 18 or older.
- Have at least six months' experience making coffee. This is not essential if you have taken a barista course.
- Be punctual and friendly with customers.

We offer:
- A one-year contract, minimum wage plus tips.
- Free training in coffee-making methods.
If you are interested, bring your CV Monday to Friday, from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m., to Calle 57 # 9-15.

questions.q: What is the advert for?
options: To advertise free coffee tastings
To find a new worker for a café
To sell coffee machines to cafés
To announce that a café is opening
questions.explain: The heading says 'SE NECESITA BARISTA', and the advert lists 'Requisitos' and what the café offers.

questions.q: How can people apply for the job?
options: Send an email before the weekend
Call the café on a Saturday morning
Fill in a form at the café on Sunday
Bring a CV on a weekday afternoon
questions.explain: The advert says 'traer la hoja de vida de lunes a viernes, de 2:00 a 5:00 p. m.'

questions.q: Who could get this job?
options: A 16-year-old with two years of experience
An adult who can only work Monday to Friday
An adult with a barista course but no experience
An adult who wants a contract for just a month
questions.explain: You must be 'mayor de edad', and experience 'no es indispensable si ha hecho un curso de barismo'.

topic: lost wallet returned by a vendor
title: El vendedor de dulces
text:
Esa mañana, en el bus, un vendedor de dulces se le acercó a Mauricio, pero él ni lo miró: iba tarde y de mal humor.

Al mediodía, se dio cuenta de que no tenía la billetera. Estaba buscándola por todas partes cuando sonó su celular. Era el vendedor del bus: había encontrado la billetera debajo de un asiento y había llamado al número de una tarjeta de presentación.

Cuando se vieron esa tarde, Mauricio le compró todos los dulces que le quedaban.
translation:
That morning, on the bus, a candy seller came up to Mauricio, but he didn't even look at him: he was running late and in a bad mood.

At noon, he realized he didn't have his wallet. He was looking for it everywhere when his phone rang. It was the seller from the bus: he had found the wallet under a seat and had called the number on a business card.

When they met that afternoon, Mauricio bought all the candy he had left.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A man who is fired for arriving late
A candy seller who opens his own shop
A man who leaves his phone on a bus
A man who gets his lost wallet back
questions.explain: Mauricio loses his wallet, and the candy seller from the bus finds it and gives it back.

questions.q: How did the seller contact Mauricio?
options: He called the number on a business card
He went to Mauricio's office downtown
He waited for him at the next bus stop
He asked the bus driver to call Mauricio
questions.explain: The seller 'había llamado al número de una tarjeta de presentación'.

questions.q: Why did Mauricio buy all the candy the seller had left?
options: He needed a present for his colleagues
He wanted to thank him for his honesty
He wanted to sell the candy at work
He had not had breakfast that morning
questions.explain: That morning Mauricio 'ni lo miró', but the seller gave his wallet back; buying all his candy is his way of saying thank you.

topic: handing over work before a vacation
title: Antes de mis vacaciones
text:
Asunto: Mis vacaciones

Hola, equipo:
Les recuerdo que estaré de vacaciones del 1 al 15 de julio. Mientras esté por fuera, Natalia se encargará de los clientes nuevos y Jorge, de las facturas. Todo lo que necesitan está en la carpeta compartida.
Si alguien pregunta por el proyecto del hotel, díganle que lo retomamos cuando yo vuelva.
Por favor, no me llamen a menos que sea algo urgente: voy a estar en una finca con poca señal.
¡Nos vemos a la vuelta!
Mónica
translation:
Subject: My vacation

Hi, team,
Just a reminder that I'll be on vacation from July 1 to 15. While I'm away, Natalia will take care of the new clients, and Jorge, the invoices. Everything you need is in the shared folder.
If anyone asks about the hotel project, tell them we'll pick it up again when I'm back.
Please don't call me unless it's something urgent: I'll be at a farm with poor signal.
See you when I get back!
Mónica

options: To organize the work during her vacation
To invite the team to a farm in July
To ask the team to finish the hotel project
To introduce two new members of the team
questions.explain: Mónica says she will be on vacation and explains who will do each task while she is away.

questions.q: Who will take care of the invoices?
options: Natalia
Jorge
Mónica herself
Natalia and Jorge
questions.explain: The email says 'Natalia se encargará de los clientes nuevos y Jorge, de las facturas'.

questions.q: A client asks about the hotel project on July 3. What should the team say?

That Mónica will call back the same day

That it will continue after July 15

topic: burnt rice at lunch with in-laws
title: El almuerzo con mis suegros
text:
Era la primera vez que mis suegros venían a almorzar a nuestro apartamento, y yo quería que todo saliera perfecto. Preparé pollo sudado y arroz con coco.

Mientras hablaba por teléfono, el arroz se me quemó. Cuando mi suegra entró a la cocina y vio la olla negra, pensé que me iba a criticar. En cambio, se rio y me contó que el día que conoció a su suegra se le quemó el pollo.

Ese día almorzamos sin arroz, pero con muchas risas.
translation:
It was the first time my in-laws were coming to lunch at our apartment, and I wanted everything to turn out perfect. I made chicken stew and coconut rice.

While I was talking on the phone, I burned the rice. When my mother-in-law came into the kitchen and saw the black pot, I thought she was going to criticize me. Instead, she laughed and told me that on the day she met her own mother-in-law, she burned the chicken.

That day we had lunch without rice, but with lots of laughter.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A big argument with the narrator's in-laws
A cooking class at the narrator's home
A lunch that goes wrong but ends well
A visit to a new restaurant downtown
questions.explain: The narrator wanted everything 'perfecto' and something went wrong, but they ate 'con muchas risas'.

questions.q: What happened while the narrator was on the phone?
options: The chicken got cold
The rice got burned
The guests came early
The salad fell over
questions.explain: The narrator says 'Mientras hablaba por teléfono, el arroz se me quemó'.

questions.q: Why did the mother-in-law tell her own story?
options: To make the narrator feel less bad
To show that she cooks much better
To ask the narrator for the recipe
To complain about her mother-in-law
questions.explain: The narrator expected criticism, but she laughed and said she had once burned the chicken herself.

topic: a week without social media
title: Una semana sin redes
text:
Lunes, 10 p. m.
Hoy empecé mi reto: una semana sin redes sociales. Borré las aplicaciones para no tener tentaciones.

Lo más difícil fue la mañana: apenas me desperté, busqué el celular por costumbre. En el bus, en vez de ver videos, miré por la ventana y descubrí un mural que nunca había visto.

Hace un rato terminé un libro que llevaba meses en la mesa de noche. No sé si voy a aguantar toda la semana, pero hoy me sentí más tranquila.
translation:
Monday, 10 p.m.
Today I started my challenge: a week without social media. I deleted the apps so I wouldn't be tempted.

The morning was the hardest part: as soon as I woke up, I reached for my phone out of habit. On the bus, instead of watching videos, I looked out of the window and discovered a mural I had never seen.

A little while ago, I finished a book that had been on my bedside table for months. I don't know if I'll last the whole week, but today I felt calmer.

questions.q: What is the diary entry about?
options: A walk to see a new mural downtown
Losing her cell phone on the bus
Her first meeting at a book club
Her first day without social media
questions.explain: She writes 'Hoy empecé mi reto: una semana sin redes sociales'.

questions.q: What did she do on the bus?
options: She read a few pages of a book
She chatted with a classmate
She looked out of the window
She listened to music on her phone
questions.explain: She writes 'en vez de ver videos, miré por la ventana'.

questions.q: She writes that the book 'llevaba meses en la mesa de noche'. What does this mean?
options: It had been by her bed for months
She had read it every night for months
She had borrowed it months ago
It was a gift from a few months ago
questions.explain: 'Llevaba meses en la mesa de noche' means the book had been lying on her bedside table for months.

topic: roommates and a high electricity bill
title: El recibo de la luz
text:
—Juli, ¿te puedo decir algo sin que te pongas brava?
—Uy, ¿qué hice?
—Nada grave. Llegó el recibo de la luz: casi el doble del mes pasado.
—¿En serio? ¿Será por el calentador nuevo?
—Puede ser, pero creo que es más por las duchas de media hora.
—Ay, ya sé que me demoro, pero es que con este frío...
—Te entiendo. ¿Qué tal si este mes lo pagamos a medias y, desde mañana, te bañas en diez minutos?
—Trato hecho, pero ponme una alarma.
translation:
—Juli, can I tell you something without you getting angry?
—Uh-oh, what did I do?
—Nothing serious. The electricity bill came: almost double last month's.
—Really? Could it be because of the new water heater?
—Maybe, but I think it's more because of the half-hour showers.
—Oh, I know I take a long time, but it's just that with this cold...
—I understand. How about we split it half and half this month and, starting tomorrow, you shower in ten minutes?
—Deal, but set an alarm for me.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Who has to clean the bathroom this week
Why the electricity bill is so high
Buying a new heater for the shower
Moving to a warmer part of the city
questions.explain: One of them says the 'recibo de la luz' is 'casi el doble del mes pasado', and they talk about why.

questions.q: What do they agree to do this month?
options: Split this month's bill in half
Ask the owner to pay part of it
Pay according to each one's use
Turn off the heater at night
questions.explain: Her roommate suggests 'este mes lo pagamos a medias', and Juli answers 'Trato hecho'.

questions.q: In the first line, what does 'ponerse brava' mean?
options: To get bored
To get cold
To get tired
To get angry
questions.explain: Juli answers '¿qué hice?', as if she were in trouble, so 'ponerse brava' means to get angry.

topic: neighbors' chat about a lost dog
title: ¿De quién es esta perrita?
text:
Patricia: Buenas noches, vecinos. En el parqueadero hay una perrita café con collar rojo, pero sin placa. ¿Alguien sabe de quién es?
Hernán: Debe ser de alguien de aquí, porque el portero dice que no ha entrado ningún perro de afuera.
Lucía: ¡Es Canela, la de los Martínez! Están de viaje y se la dejaron a la sobrina. Se le habrá escapado cuando sacó la basura.
Lucía: Ya le escribí. Dice que baja en cinco minutos.
Patricia: ¡Menos mal!
translation:
Patricia: Good evening, neighbors. In the parking lot there's a little brown dog with a red collar, but no tag. Does anyone know whose she is?
Hernán: She must belong to someone here, because the doorman says no dog has come in from outside.
Lucía: It's Canela, the Martínez family's dog! They're away on a trip and left her with their niece. She must have got out when the niece took out the trash.
Lucía: I've already texted her. She says she'll be down in five minutes.
Patricia: That's a relief!

questions.q: What is the chat mainly about?
options: Finding out who a lost dog belongs to
Complaints about a dog barking at night
A neighbor's plans for a trip abroad
New rules for the building's parking lot
questions.explain: Patricia found a dog in the parking lot and asks '¿Alguien sabe de quién es?'

questions.q: Why does Hernán think the dog lives in the building?
options: He has seen it in the elevator
Its tag has the building's address
The doorman says no dog came in
He recognizes its red collar
questions.explain: Hernán writes 'el portero dice que no ha entrado ningún perro de afuera'.

questions.q: How does Lucía think the dog ended up alone?
options: The Martínez family left it there alone
A neighbor brought it in from the busy street
The doorman let it in through the main door
It got out when the niece took out the trash
questions.explain: Lucía writes 'Se le habrá escapado cuando sacó la basura': it probably got away from the niece then.

topic: asking a professor for an extension
title: Un correo a la profesora
text:
Asunto: Solicitud de más plazo para el trabajo final

Estimada profesora Gómez:
Le escribo porque el martes se me dañó el computador y perdí casi todo el trabajo final de Historia del Arte, que debía entregar este viernes. Ya lo estoy escribiendo de nuevo, pero no alcanzo a terminarlo a tiempo.
Por esta razón, le agradecería mucho que me permitiera entregarlo el lunes. Adjunto la constancia del técnico.
Entiendo si no es posible hacer una excepción.
Cordialmente,
Daniela Torres
translation:
Subject: Request for an extension on the final paper

Dear Professor Gómez,
I'm writing because on Tuesday my computer broke down and I lost almost all of my final paper for Art History, which I was supposed to hand in this Friday. I'm already writing it again, but I won't manage to finish it in time.
For this reason, I would be very grateful if you would allow me to hand it in on Monday. I'm attaching the technician's report.
I understand if it isn't possible to make an exception.
Best regards,
Daniela Torres

questions.q: Why does Daniela write to her professor?
options: To say that she is leaving the course
To invite the professor to an exhibition
To ask for more time to hand in her work
To ask if she can change her paper's topic
questions.explain: She asks 'le agradecería mucho que me permitiera entregarlo el lunes'.

questions.q: When was Daniela supposed to hand in her work?
options: Last Tuesday
Next Monday
In two weeks
This Friday
questions.explain: She writes that she 'debía entregar este viernes'.

questions.q: Why does Daniela attach the technician's report?
options: To ask her to pay for the repair
To show that her story is true
To prove that she finished the work
To recommend a good repair shop
questions.explain: A 'constancia del técnico' is written proof from the repair person that her computer really broke.

topic: elevator breakdown before a meeting
title: Atrapados en el ascensor
text:
Clara llevaba diez minutos encerrada en el ascensor con un señor de corbata. Tenía una reunión con un cliente nuevo a las nueve, y ya eran las nueve y cinco.

El señor, en cambio, estaba tranquilo. Le preguntó a qué se dedicaba, y ella le habló de su empresa como si estuvieran en una entrevista.

Cuando por fin se abrió la puerta, los dos caminaron hacia la misma sala de reuniones.
—Bueno —dijo él, sonriendo—, ya me contó todo lo que necesitaba saber.
translation:
Clara had been stuck in the elevator for ten minutes with a man in a tie. She had a meeting with a new client at nine, and it was already five past nine.

The man, on the other hand, was calm. He asked her what she did for a living, and she told him about her company as if they were in an interview.

When the door finally opened, the two of them walked toward the same meeting room.
“Well,” he said with a smile, “you've already told me everything I needed to know.”

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A job interview that goes very badly
A woman who is afraid of small spaces
A woman who loses her job for arriving late
An elevator delay with a surprise ending
questions.explain: Clara is stuck in an elevator with a man, and at the end she finds out who he is.

questions.q: Why was Clara worried about the time?
options: She had a job interview at nine
She had a nine o'clock meeting
She had to catch a flight at nine
She had to pick up her son at nine
questions.explain: She had 'una reunión... a las nueve', and it was already 'las nueve y cinco'.

questions.q: Who was the man in the elevator?
options: A technician who fixes elevators
Clara's new boss at the company
The client Clara was going to meet
A doorman from the building
questions.explain: They walk to 'la misma sala de reuniones', and he says she has already told him 'todo lo que necesitaba saber'.

topic: brake repair at a car mechanic
title: En el taller
text:
—Don Álvaro, ¿qué tiene el carro?
—Le cuento: el ruido que usted oía al frenar viene de las pastillas, que están gastadas.
—¿Y es grave?
—Todavía no, pero si yo fuera usted, no esperaría mucho. Si se dañan los discos, le sale mucho más caro.
—¿Y cuánto me cuesta cambiarlas?
—Con mano de obra, unos trescientos mil pesos. Se lo tengo listo mañana al mediodía.
—Hágale. Pero ¿no habrá forma de que me lo entregue hoy? Es que mañana salgo temprano para Girardot.
translation:
—Don Álvaro, what's wrong with the car?
—Here's the thing: the noise you heard when braking comes from the brake pads, which are worn out.
—And is it serious?
—Not yet, but if I were you, I wouldn't wait long. If the discs get damaged, it'll cost you much more.
—And how much does it cost to replace them?
—With labor, about three hundred thousand pesos. I'll have it ready for you tomorrow at noon.
—Go ahead. But isn't there any way you could have it ready for me today? The thing is, I'm leaving early tomorrow for Girardot.

questions.q: What are the customer and the mechanic talking about?
options: A problem with the car's brakes
Buying a new car for a long trip
A noise coming from the car's engine
Directions for driving to Girardot
questions.explain: The mechanic says the noise 'al frenar' comes from 'las pastillas', which are worn out.

questions.q: When does the mechanic say the car will be ready?
options: Later this afternoon
Early tomorrow
In three days
Tomorrow at noon
questions.explain: Don Álvaro says 'Se lo tengo listo mañana al mediodía'.

questions.q: What does the customer mean by 'Hágale'?
options: That's much too expensive
OK, go ahead and do it
I need to think about it
I'll do the repair myself
questions.explain: After hearing the price, the customer says 'Hágale' and only asks if the car can be ready today, so he agrees to the repair.

topic: taking the wrong bus by mistake
title: El bus equivocado
text:
Manuel llevaba quince años tomando el mismo bus para ir al trabajo, así que el día en que se equivocó de ruta tardó un buen rato en darse cuenta. Cuando al fin levantó la vista del celular, estaba en un barrio que no conocía.

Se bajó, molesto, y entró a una panadería a preguntar cómo volver. Allí probó unas almojábanas idénticas a las que le hacía su abuela cuando era niño.

Desde entonces, todos los viernes se «equivoca» de bus a propósito.
translation:
Manuel had been taking the same bus to work for fifteen years, so on the day he took the wrong route, it took him a good while to notice. When he finally looked up from his phone, he was in a neighborhood he didn't know.

He got off, annoyed, and went into a bakery to ask how to get back. There he tried some almojábanas (cheese bread rolls) identical to the ones his grandmother used to make him when he was a boy.

Since then, every Friday he “takes the wrong bus” on purpose.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A man who is late for an important meeting
A mistake that leads to a nice discovery
A man who moves to a new neighborhood
A bus driver who gets lost in the city
questions.explain: Manuel takes the wrong bus by mistake, and the day ends with a pleasant surprise.

questions.q: What was Manuel doing on the bus?
options: Sleeping in the back seat
Talking with the driver
Looking at his cell phone
Reading a book for work
questions.explain: The text says 'Cuando al fin levantó la vista del celular', so he had been looking at his phone.

questions.q: Why does Manuel take the 'wrong' bus every Friday?
options: He wants to go back to that bakery
He still mixes up the two bus routes
His office moved to that neighborhood
His usual bus no longer runs on Fridays
questions.explain: The quotation marks and 'a propósito' show he does it on purpose: he goes back for the almojábanas like his grandmother's.
